criteria.no: It contains at least two duties that a plan or implementation could satisfy or violate independently.
criteria.unclear: The wording is too ambiguous to determine how many independent duties it contains.
criteria.yes: It contains one obligation; removing a clause would narrow that obligation rather than remove a separately satisfiable duty.

atomic-a-independent-obligation.instructions: Does anchor.statement impose one independently satisfiable obligation or prohibition? A condition, exception, or several evidence surfaces may belong to one obligation. Judge atomicity only.

criteria.no: It can be split into two or more constraints that could receive different outcomes.
criteria.unclear: Possible clauses exist, but their independence cannot be determined from the statement.
criteria.yes: There is no useful split into constraints that could receive different outcomes.

atomic-b-separability.instructions: Can anchor.statement be kept as one atomic anchor, rather than split into two constraints with different pass/fail outcomes? Treat input/action/outcome detail and enumerated output surfaces as detail of one constraint.

criteria.no: Yes; the statement expresses multiple requirements with separable satisfaction outcomes.
criteria.unclear: The statement does not make the requirement boundaries clear enough to decide.
criteria.yes: No; the statement expresses one requirement, possibly with conditions or multiple places where the same outcome must hold.

atomic-c-counterfactual.instructions: Could the system satisfy one requirement in anchor.statement while violating another requirement in the same statement? Judge only whether the statement bundles requirements.

criteria.no: The statement adds, changes, or reverses an obligation beyond what the quote supports.
criteria.unclear: The quote is too ambiguous to determine whether it supports the statement's obligation.
criteria.yes: The quote supports the statement's complete obligation, and the statement adds no unsupported policy or mechanism.

faithful-a-supported-obligation.instructions: Is every obligation in anchor.statement supported by anchor.quote without changing what the quote requires or forbids? An atomic statement may capture one directive from a multi-directive quote without restating unrelated directives.

criteria.no: Accepting the statement requires an extra policy, mechanism, strength, or outcome not present in the quote.
criteria.unclear: The quote admits materially different readings, so entailment cannot be settled.
criteria.yes: The statement follows from the quote without an extra product or implementation decision.

faithful-b-entailment.instructions: Read anchor.quote in its ordinary context. Does it entail the constraint written in anchor.statement? It need not entail that unrelated directives from the same quote are also part of this atomic anchor.

criteria.no: At least one element of the statement lacks support or conflicts with the quote.
criteria.unclear: The quote does not provide enough meaning to verify support.
criteria.yes: Each element of the statement has direct support in the quote; unrelated quoted directives may be separate anchors.

faithful-c-proof-burden.instructions: Can the author justify every required or forbidden element of anchor.statement directly from anchor.quote? Judge source support only, not whether the statement is testable.

criteria.no: It asks only for a subjective quality, preference, or intention with no checkable outcome.
criteria.unclear: It hints at evidence but does not define enough to know what would demonstrate compliance.
criteria.yes: A reviewer can identify evidence that would show whether the stated behavior or artifact exists.

observable-a-evidence.instructions: Does anchor.statement identify behavior or an artifact whose presence, absence, value, location, order, or output can be checked? Do not require literal token matching; judge observability only.

criteria.no: No concrete observation could distinguish compliance from noncompliance.
criteria.unclear: The statement is partly concrete, but what observation settles it remains ambiguous.
criteria.yes: At least one concrete observation could show the statement met or broken.

observable-b-falsifiable.instructions: Is anchor.statement falsifiable from a plan, diff, test, command result, or recorded artifact? Judge the claimed outcome, not grammar or source fidelity.

criteria.no: The result depends on taste or an undefined quality rather than observable evidence.
criteria.unclear: Some objective detail exists, but the decisive evidence is not identifiable.
criteria.yes: The statement supplies an objective behavior or artifact to inspect.

observable-c-reviewer.instructions: Could two reviewers inspect the same relevant evidence and apply anchor.statement to reach a result based on behavior or artifacts rather than taste? Judge only the existence of an observable check.

criteria.no: No governed area is identified, so applicability to a plan item or change cannot be determined.
criteria.unclear: A possible area is suggested, but its applicability boundary remains ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The governed component, activity, artifact, command set, or explicit global boundary is identifiable.

scoped-a-applicability.instructions: Using anchor.statement together with anchor.scope, can a reviewer decide whether a particular plan item or change falls within this anchor? A deliberately global scope is identifiable and may pass.

criteria.no: The constraint floats without a component, activity, artifact, or global boundary.
criteria.unclear: The boundary is partially described but cannot be applied consistently.
criteria.yes: The applicability boundary is named or clearly implied, even if it is intentionally global.

scoped-b-boundary.instructions: Do anchor.statement and anchor.scope establish an identifiable boundary for where the constraint applies, including an explicit all-system or all-command boundary? Judge scope only.

criteria.no: They provide no usable governed area for that classification.
criteria.unclear: They name an area, but leave material cases impossible to classify.
criteria.yes: The statement and scope support a repeatable inside/outside classification; an explicit global scope puts all relevant work inside.

scoped-c-classification.instructions: Could a reviewer classify candidate work as inside or outside anchor.statement's governed area from anchor.statement plus anchor.scope?

criteria.no: Applying it requires private shorthand, an undefined term, or an approval/decision that is neither specified nor recorded.
criteria.unclear: Most conditions are stated, but at least one dependency may require outside interpretation.
criteria.yes: All terms and conditions needed to apply the constraint are stated or point to recorded, identifiable evidence.

self-a-recorded-conditions.instructions: Are the conditions and terms in anchor.statement decidable from the statement and recorded project artifacts, without private shorthand or an unrecorded future approval? Explicit prohibitions and input/action/outcome conditions may pass.

criteria.no: The reviewer must obtain unstated meaning or an unrecorded decision before applying it.
criteria.unclear: The reviewer can apply part of it, but a material term or condition remains open.
criteria.yes: The statement supplies enough meaning to apply its direct requirement, prohibition, or explicit test condition.

self-b-independent-reader.instructions: Can an independent reviewer apply anchor.statement without asking its author what shorthand, quality, exception, or approval means? Judge self-containment only.

criteria.no: A decision input is private, undefined, or dependent on an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: A decision input is mentioned but not specified well enough to use.
criteria.yes: Its decision inputs are explicit or recorded and its condition has a checkable trigger and outcome.

self-c-decision-inputs.instructions: Does anchor.statement contain or identify every input needed to decide compliance, including any exception or condition? A concrete never/must-not prohibition is self-contained even though it is negative.

criteria.no: One of those elements depends on private shorthand, undefined quality, or unrecorded consent.
criteria.unclear: The operational meaning is partially present but not settled.
criteria.yes: The trigger, subject, and outcome are explicit enough for independent application; unconditional constraints need no artificial trigger.

self-d-operational.instructions: Does anchor.statement stand on its own as an operational constraint: a reviewer knows the trigger, governed subject, and required or forbidden outcome without external conversation?

anchor.quote: test a transport failure with a canary TypeSafe key and make sure console output and saved run files contain neither the key nor its bearer header
anchor.scope: transport-error output and persisted run artifacts
anchor.statement: When TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set to canary-123 and transport fails, stdout, stderr, and saved run artifacts must omit canary-123 and Authorization: Bearer canary-123.
